Munson expands medical drone trials to multiple aircraft and longer flights

Phase two in Michigan runs October 6–30, simulating transport of supplies, lab samples and medicines to gather evidence for rural healthcare logistics.

sUAS News ↗5 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Linking healthcare facilities in a trial

An October 5 announcement describes the second project phase led by Traverse Connect, Munson Healthcare, blueflite and Central Michigan University’s Rural Health Excellence Institute. Flights between Munson Medical Center and Crystal Lake Health Center are scheduled for October 6–30. They simulate supplies, laboratory samples and medication transport rather than constitute a complete routine medical-delivery network.

Building beyond the first phase

The May 9–20, 2025 phase completed nearly 70 flights within a one-mile radius of Munson Medical Center. The new phase extends flight duration and introduces multiple aircraft and sensor technology. The partners report FAA approval, but the announcement does not list every operational condition and should not be read as permission for unrestricted flights anywhere.

Evidence before broader deployment

The pilot collects operating data to assess how air transport can connect rural healthcare facilities. Support comes from Michigan’s Advanced Aerial Mobility Activation Fund and Newlab. Phase-two results are intended to inform scaling decisions; there are not yet reported outcome figures from this phase showing reductions in treatment time, cost or errors.
